q: בן 78, אושפז לברור עקב קושי בבליעת מוצקים וירידה במשקל. הועלה חשד לקרצינומה של הוושט. מהם גורמי הסיכון לאדנוקרצינומה של הוושט בגיל המבוגר?
o: טיפול ממושך ב- PPI's
שתיית אלכוהול
רקע של Barrett esophagus

explanation:
Esophageal adenocarcinoma can develop in metaplastic epithelium associated with chronic reflux. **Barrett esophagus** is the characteristic precursor in an older person with progressive dysphagia and weight loss.

**A. Long-term PPI use.** Acid suppression treats reflux accompanying Barrett esophagus. It is not the precursor lesion.
**B. Alcohol.** Its stronger histologic association is with squamous cell carcinoma.
**C. Barrett esophagus.** Intestinal metaplasia can progress through dysplasia to adenocarcinoma.
**D. Achalasia.** Its cancer risk is predominantly squamous, although a smaller increase in adenocarcinoma has also been documented.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1322, 1449. ACG Clinical Guidelines for Achalasia, 2020, p. 1407.
Key note: Barrett esophagus was accepted. The ACG guideline also reports an increase in adenocarcinoma risk with achalasia, substantially smaller than its squamous cancer risk.

q: A comprehensive geriatric assessment team has implemented a care plan and is following the patient. Progress toward the agreed goals is inadequate. Which response is part of the CGA process described in Hazzard?
o: Count documented problems to assess implementation.
Count recommendations completed by the team.
Review outcomes with the patient and revise the plan.
Count new specialist referrals generated by the assessment.
explanation:
Monitoring tests whether a plan was implemented and whether the patient is reaching the agreed goals. **If progress falls short, reassess with the patient, revise the plan and follow the response.**

**A. Count documented problems to assess implementation** — A problem list describes findings. Its length says nothing about recovery or independence.
**B. Count recommendations completed by the team** — Advice delivered may never have been feasible to carry out. Ask what actually happened.
**C. Review outcomes with the patient and revise the plan** — Check implementation, barriers, clinical changes and whether the patient's priorities have changed.
**D. Count new specialist referrals generated by the assessment** — Additional referrals can help an identified need, but their number cannot measure the patient's outcome.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 130, Monitoring and Revising the Treatment Plan.

q: A 76-year-old woman with dementia, diabetes, and hypertension undergoes comprehensive geriatric assessment. Her adult son is her principal caregiver. Which approach best incorporates patient-centered care into the treatment plan?
o: Use motivational interviewing to secure agreement with goals already chosen by the team
Use motivational interviewing to identify her priorities and willingness to make changes
Use the diagnosis list to set disease-based goals before discussing the plan with her son
Use her son's preferences to set goals and judge success by adherence to instructions
explanation:
Patient-centered planning starts with what the person hopes to achieve and what changes are acceptable. **Use motivational interviewing to elicit her own priorities and readiness, involving her son as appropriate.**

**A. Obtain agreement** — Persuading her to accept predetermined goals misses the purpose of the conversation.
**B. Elicit priorities and readiness** — Questions about what matters to her and what she feels able to change help shape a feasible plan.
**C. Disease targets first** — Separate disease targets can compete. Her goals help the team decide which interventions to prioritize.
**D. Caregiver sets goals** — Her son can provide observations and practical help. Dementia alone does not remove her role in decisions.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 130, Development of the Treatment Plan.
ref: Hazzard Ch 8 — PRINCIPLES OF GERIATRIC ASSESSMENT

q: A 76-year-old man with benign prostatic hyperplasia is undergoing a trial without catheter. He has difficulty voiding and a postvoid residual of 650 mL. Glucose and oxygen saturation are normal, and he is stable. Which action addresses this residual according to the bladder-retraining protocol in Hazzard?
o: Reinsert a Foley catheter and plan another voiding trial
Lengthen the intervals between voids and monitor a bladder diary
Start a bladder relaxant and monitor urinary symptoms
Reduce daily fluid intake and remeasure the residual later
explanation:
A failed trial without catheter can leave a large volume behind the outlet. **Reinsert a Foley for a 650 mL residual and retry voiding after several days.**

**A. Reinsert a Foley catheter and plan another voiding trial** — This volume exceeds the protocol’s 300 to 400 mL threshold for Foley drainage.
**B. Lengthen the intervals between voids and monitor a bladder diary** — Spacing voids addresses frequency in a bladder that empties adequately.
**C. Start a bladder relaxant and monitor urinary symptoms** — A bladder relaxant may aggravate the retention.
**D. Reduce daily fluid intake and remeasure the residual later** — Restricting fluids cannot drain urine that has already accumulated.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, Ch. 47, p. 711, Table 47-11.

q: An 81-year-old woman has lost about 8 lb and feels fatigued over recent months. She lives with her daughter, who works full time, and spends most days alone watching television and eating microwave meals. BMI is 19.5 and albumin 3.1 g/dL; PHQ-2 is negative, and the Berkman-Syme social network index indicates marked isolation. Which plan directly addresses mealtime isolation as part of nutritional care?
o: Prescribe an oral nutritional supplement.
Arrange home delivery of prepared meals.
Trial an appetite stimulant.
Arrange a shared meal program at a senior center.
explanation:
A meal program can address food access, companionship or both. **Shared lunches at a senior center directly address her marked mealtime isolation.**

**A. Prescribe an oral nutritional supplement** — They may add energy, but they do not bring another person to the table.
**B. Arrange home delivery of prepared meals** — Delivery helps with shopping and preparation. In this version of the plan, social isolation continues.
**C. Trial an appetite stimulant** — Drug treatment leaves the social barrier in place and can introduce serious adverse effects.
**D. Arrange a shared meal program at a senior center** — This provides a meal and people to eat with. Follow intake, weight and the remaining causes of weight loss.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 409–410 and 427, determinants of intake and feeding assistance.
ref: Hazzard Ch 30 — NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION

q: An 88-year-old woman with advanced COPD is seen in palliative care. She uses continuous oxygen and a wheelchair and needs assistance with all activities of daily living. Because of treatment burden, she asks to stop her medications, including prednisone taken daily for two years. What approach applies if chronic prednisone is discontinued?
o: Stop prednisone and monitor respiratory symptoms.
Stop prednisone and restart it if fatigue appears.
Taper prednisone to allow adrenal-axis recovery.
Reserve corticosteroid replacement for a future illness.
explanation:
Daily prednisone can suppress endogenous ACTH and cortisol production for months. **If her goals and respiratory status allow withdrawal after two years, taper gradually and reassess as the dose approaches physiologic replacement.**

**A. Stop prednisone and monitor respiratory symptoms** — Monitoring COPD alone misses hypotension, weakness and gastrointestinal symptoms from cortisol deficiency.
**B. Stop prednisone and restart it if fatigue appears** — Fatigue is nonspecific and an adrenal crisis may develop before a trial of oral prednisone is practical.
**C. Taper prednisone to allow adrenal-axis recovery** — A tailored taper reduces the risk of symptomatic deficiency while the adrenal axis recovers and allows respiratory symptoms to guide comfort care.
**D. Reserve corticosteroid replacement for a future illness** — Basal cortisol can already be inadequate during withdrawal even before a new stressor occurs.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1531–1532. ESE/Endocrine Society glucocorticoid-induced adrenal insufficiency guideline (2024), recommendations 2.2–2.8.
ref: Hazzard Ch 97 — AGING OF THE ENDOCRINE SYSTEM AND NON-THYROID ENDOCRINE DISORDERS

o: להסיק שסירוב להארכת חיים מחייב מניעת כל טיפול
לכבד רצון ולעשות מאמץ סביר לשכנע לקבל טיפול
להתחיל טיפול בזיהום בהתעלם מהסירוב שהביעה
להעביר לבני המשפחה את ההחלטה במקום החולה
explanation:
מכבדים החלטה מודעת של חולה כשירה הנוטה למות. יש לעשות מאמץ סביר לשכנע אותה לקבל טיפול מקל וטיפול נלווה, לרבות טיפול בזיהום שאינו קשור למחלה חשוכת המרפא. **לכבד רצון ולעשות מאמץ סביר לשכנע לקבל טיפול**.

**א. להסיק שסירוב להארכת חיים מחייב מניעת כל טיפול.** סירוב להארכת חיים אינו שולל אוטומטית טיפול בזיהום.
**ב. לכבד רצון ולעשות מאמץ סביר לשכנע לקבל טיפול.** מסבירים מדוע הטיפול מוצע ומבררים את בחירתה.
**ג. להתחיל טיפול בזיהום בהתעלם מהסירוב שהביעה.** אין לכפות את הטיפול על סמך סיווגו בלבד.
**ד. להעביר לבני המשפחה את ההחלטה במקום החולה.** החולה עצמה מוסמכת להכריע כשהיא כשירה.

q: An 83-year-old woman with COPD experiences dyspnea during rehabilitation. Which breathing modification is described in Hazzard as a way to reduce the sensation of breathlessness?
o: Exhale briefly through pursed lips
Exhale slowly through pursed lips
Take short breaths through an open mouth
Increase breathing frequency during exertion
explanation:
Breathing retraining can reduce perceived breathlessness in COPD. **Pursed-lip breathing with prolonged exhalation** gives more time for lung emptying during rehabilitation.

**A. Pursed lips and short expiration.** Shortening the phase loses the intended expiratory benefit.
**B. Pursed lips and prolonged expiration.** A slow, controlled breath out can help reduce air trapping.
**C. Open mouth and short expiration.** This lacks the controlled expiratory pattern.
**D. Faster breathing.** Short rapid breaths can worsen dynamic hyperinflation.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1074.
ref: Hazzard Ch 69 — MANAGEMENT OF COMMON NONPAIN SYMPTOMS

. Faster breathing.** Short rapid breaths can worsen dynamic hyperinflation.

q: An older patient with renal failure takes a serotonergic antidepressant. Which precaution is most relevant before prescribing tramadol?
o: The combination lowers serotonergic toxicity, allowing dose escalation.
Tramadol does not require a renal adjustment if liver tests are normal.
Consider serotonergic toxicity and adjust tramadol for renal function.
Monitoring for respiratory depression replaces review of antidepressant interactions.
explanation:
Tramadol has opioid and monoamine effects. **Combining it with a serotonergic antidepressant raises serotonin syndrome risk, and renal failure requires dose adjustment.**

**A. The combination lowers serotonergic toxicity, allowing dose escalation** — A serotonergic antidepressant adds risk when combined with tramadol. It does not protect against toxicity.
**B. Tramadol does not require a renal adjustment if liver tests are normal** — Renal impairment can delay elimination even if liver tests are normal.
**C. Consider serotonergic toxicity and adjust tramadol for renal function** — Review the serotonergic interaction and the dose or interval appropriate to renal function and formulation.
**D. Monitoring for respiratory depression replaces review of antidepressant interactions** — Monitoring opioid effects is important but cannot substitute for identifying the serotonergic interaction.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1653.
ref: Hazzard Ch 103 — FIBROMYALGIA AND MYOFASCIAL PAIN SYNDROMES

q: בת 75, ברקע. דמנציה, דיכאון, סוכרת, יתר לחץ דם ואוסטאוארטריטיס. התקבלה למחלקה לרפואה דחופה. עקב החמרה בתפקודי כליה בבדיקות המעבדה נמצאה אי ספיקה כלייתית עם קריאטינין 2.3 ו- BUN - 70. בבדיקה לפני חצי שנה- קריאטינין 1.2 ו- BUN תקין. מתוך כל התרופות שלקחה בביתה – כולן יכולות לגרום לאי ספיקה כלייתית חדה פרט ל-
o: Etoricoxib ( ארקוקסיה)
Empagliflozin ( ג'רדיינס)
Candesartan ( אטקנד)
Ecitralopam ( ציפרלקס)
explanation:
When a patient's creatinine rises, look for drugs that reduce glomerular perfusion or worsen volume depletion. Of these choices, **escitalopram is the exception to this typical AKI mechanism**.

**A. Etoricoxib** — This COX-2 inhibitor decreases renal prostaglandin synthesis, impairing the afferent vasodilation needed to maintain filtration during volume depletion.
**B. Empagliflozin** — Glucose excretion in the urine can increase fluid losses. Volume depletion may contribute to acute kidney injury in a susceptible patient despite the drug's long-term kidney benefits.
**C. Candesartan** — An ARB dilates the efferent arteriole and can cause a substantial fall in filtration during low renal perfusion or bilateral renal artery stenosis.
**D. Escitalopram** — This SSRI does not ordinarily produce the renal hemodynamic changes described here. Hyponatremia is an important electrolyte adverse effect in older patients.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1279–1282, CKD Management and Table 83-1. Empagliflozin and escitalopram prescribing information, Volume Depletion and Hyponatremia.

explanation:
Both a faint and a generalized tonic-clonic seizure can cause loss of consciousness and brief jerking. **Muscle soreness after the event favors a generalized tonic-clonic seizure**, especially with prolonged disorientation, although soreness alone is not diagnostic.

**A. Rapid awakening** — Prompt recovery of awareness is more characteristic of syncope than of a postictal state.
**B. Muscle soreness** — Sustained tonic and clonic contractions can leave the muscles aching after a seizure.
**C. Blurred vision before collapse** — Dimming or tunneling of vision is a common prodrome of cerebral hypoperfusion.
**D. Motor activity lasting under ten seconds** — Brief jerks can accompany a faint. Their presence alone does not identify epilepsy.

Reference · Harrison’s Principles of Internal Medicine, 21e, pp. 3315–3316, Table 425-7.

o: פעילות גופנית יכולה להחמיר תפקוד חדר שמאל ולכן לא מומלצת
פעילות גופנית יכולה לשפר תפקוד ותחושת well being אבל לא משפרת קוצר נשימה

explanation:
Exercise in compensated heart failure improves the efficiency of active muscle and tolerance of ordinary activity. Before starting, confirm that symptoms and fluid status have been stable for several weeks.

**Structured exercise can improve quality of life and may reduce mortality. A low ejection fraction alone is no reason to withhold training when the patient is clinically stable.**

**A. Exercise worsens left ventricular function.** In appropriately selected stable patients, supervised training improves tolerance without evidence of worsening ventricular function. Prolonged inactivity instead promotes deconditioning.
**B. Function improves but dyspnea does not.** As the same workload takes a smaller fraction of the patient’s capacity, breathlessness and fatigue during daily activities can improve.
**C. Better quality of life and possible survival benefit.** Functional and symptom benefits are consistent. Lower mortality has been reported in some exercise-based rehabilitation studies, without implying a guaranteed benefit for this patient.
**D. Resistance work only.** Aerobic training is an appropriate component of rehabilitation. Resistance work can be added according to strength, symptoms and tolerance.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 830, 1177–1178.

o: תרופות ממשפחת ה- Tricyclics מהוות קו ראשון לטיפול בכאב נוירופתי
ל- Venlafaxine יתרון בטיחותי במניעת נפילות ושברים
לטיפול ב- Carbamazepine סיכון להיפונתרמיה
טיפול ב- Gabapentin מחייב מעקב הדוק אחר רמות תרופה בדם
explanation:
Adjuvant analgesics treat particular pain mechanisms and require drug-specific monitoring. **Carbamazepine can cause hyponatremia. Check sodium when starting it and during follow-up.**

**A. Tricyclics as routine first-line treatment** They can relieve neuropathic pain, but anticholinergic toxicity and falls limit their suitability for older adults.
**B. Venlafaxine protects against falls and fractures** SNRIs can contribute to falls. A fall or fracture history increases concern.
**C. Carbamazepine and low sodium** New confusion, weakness or unsteadiness can be a clue. Also review blood count, interactions and other appropriate laboratory monitoring.
**D. Routine gabapentin levels** Follow renal function, alertness, gait and clinical response. Routine serum gabapentin concentrations are unnecessary for analgesic titration.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1063–1065, Table 68-8.

q: An older inpatient develops delirium after several psychoactive medications are added. Which interpretation best explains why these drugs need review?
o: Medication effects and interactions represent a potentially remediable precipitant of delirium.
Medication effects and interactions usually leave a persistent, nonremediable cause of delirium.
Increasing the number of prescribed drugs tends to reduce delirium through offsetting effects.
Drug interactions explain delirium better because the drugs themselves lack direct effects.
explanation:
Centrally acting medicines can directly alter attention, and multiple drugs create opportunities for drug–drug and drug–disease interactions. Medication exposure is often modifiable.
**Reconcile the new psychoactive drugs and assess their individual and combined effects.**

**A. Medication effects and interactions represent a potentially remediable precipitant of delirium.** Removing or reducing unnecessary exposure can address a remediable precipitant.
**B. Medication effects and interactions usually leave a persistent, nonremediable cause of delirium.** Drug effects are often among the more readily corrected contributors to delirium.
**C. Increasing the number of prescribed drugs tends to reduce delirium through offsetting effects.** Additional drugs increase exposure and interaction risk. They do not reliably offset one another.
**D. Drug interactions explain delirium better because the drugs themselves lack direct effects.** Direct effects and interactions both matter, even when a single drug has been added.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 882

q: An older community-dwelling person reports a stair fall during the past year and performs poorly on a balance test. Which next step follows the chapter’s approach?
o: Use the initial screening score to select the intervention before assessing contributing deficits.
Assess contributing deficits further to develop an individualized fall prevention care plan.
Schedule reassessment after a second fall to establish the need for a prevention care plan.
Use a predictive TUG cutoff to select the intervention after documenting the fall history.
explanation:
A fall within the past year plus poor balance performance identifies someone who needs a closer look at the cause. **Assess the contributing deficits and use them to design an individualized plan.**

**A. Choose treatment from the screen alone** — A screen identifies people needing assessment. The same poor result can arise from weakness, sensory loss or medication effects.
**B. Investigate contributors** — Examine transfers, gait, strength and vision, review medications and the stair environment, and select appropriate interventions.
**C. Wait for a second fall** — The combination of one fall and abnormal performance already warrants assessment.
**D. Select treatment from a TUG cutoff** — No universally predictive community TUG cutoff was supported. Timing alone cannot select a treatment.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 637.

q: בת 72, פליטה מאוקראינה, ללא היסטוריה רפואית ידועה, לדבריה בריאה בדרך כלל, לא שותה הרבה אלכוהול, וללא טיפול תרופתי קבוע. הופנתה בשל הרגשה כללית רעה מזה 2-3 ימים. בבדיקות הדם הפרעה משולבת באנזימי כבד. אילו מהממצאים הבאים מכוונים לכך שמדובר בהפרעה ממושכת, ולא אקוטית?
o: רמת ALT גבוהה יותר מאשר AST.
הפרעה בתפקודי קרישה
רמה תקינה של אמוניה
רמת אלבומין מתחת ל 3 gr/dL
chapterTitle: Harrison 22e ch. 348 – Evaluation of Liver Function
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q124
explanation:
Albumin is synthesized by the liver and turns over over several weeks. **An albumin below 3 g/dL is a clue to pre-existing liver disease** when the apparent illness is only two days old. Other causes of hypoalbuminemia still need consideration.

**A. ALT above AST.** This ratio can occur in acute hepatocellular injury and does not date the process.
**B. Abnormal coagulation.** Short-lived clotting factors can fall rapidly in severe acute hepatic failure.
**C. Normal ammonia.** Ammonia is an unreliable measure of chronicity and does not exclude significant liver disease.
**D. Marked hypoalbuminemia.** Slow turnover makes a major fall less likely to be explained by a brief isolated hepatic insult.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 2635–2637.

. Marked hypoalbuminemia.** Slow turnover makes a major fall less likely to be explained by a brief isolated hepatic insult.

q:
בן 78, ברקע יתר לחץ דם, דיכאון וסוכרת עבר בירור להפרעות שינה ואובחן כסובל מ- Obstructive Sleep Apnea ברמה חמורה. ניסה טיפול ב- CPAP שהופסק אחרי שבוע עקב אי סבילות.
מה ניתן להציע לו?
o: התייעצות מומחה להתאמת ה- CPAP
טיפול תרופתי ב- ZOPICLONE (NOCTURNO)
טיפול תרופתי ב- CLONAZEPAM (CLONEX)
יעוץ אף אוזן גרון בשאלה של ניתוח
keySource: IMA 2024-May Basic official answer key after appeals, Q103
explanation:
Severe obstructive sleep apnea requires effective treatment even when a first CPAP trial is uncomfortable. **Specialist adjustment of CPAP and, for selected persistent intolerance, surgical evaluation** are both reasonable routes.

**A. Specialist CPAP support.** Troubleshoot mask, pressure, leaks and nasal symptoms after a short unsuccessful trial.
**B. Zopiclone.** A hypnotic treats sleep symptoms but does not splint open an obstructed airway.
**C. Clonazepam.** Sedation does not correct obstruction and can add respiratory and fall risk.
**D. ENT surgical assessment.** Selected patients who cannot tolerate effective positive-pressure treatment may have an anatomic target. Evaluation does not guarantee that surgery will help.

Reference · Harrison 22e, p. 2281.
